log.text: Gholdengo used Make It Rain → Floette
Floette used Light of Ruin → Incineroar
Gholdengo used Make It Rain → Garchomp

decisions.rationale: Mega is Swampert. Lead Incineroar+Gholdengo: Fake Out (+3 prio) flinches a threat while Gholdengo Make It Rain hits Floette SE and resists both Fairy and Dragon. Incineroar Parting Shot pivots into Pelipper+Swampert once Altaria (Cloud Nine) is gone, enabling rain+Swift Swim sweep. Swampert-Mega Ice Punch 4x KOs Garchomp. Avoid Intimidate into Annihilape (Defiant) and Dragapult (Clear Body).
decisions.notebook: Opponent team: Floette-Eternal is their Mega (Floettite, Timid 106-158 speed, Light of Ruin 140 BP Fairy 90% acc). Altaria has Cloud Nine (shuts weather) + Focus Sash + Tailwind — primary rain counter. Annihilape has Defiant (Intimidate gives +2 Atk). Dragapult has Clear Body (immune to Intimidate) + 161-213 speed. Garchomp Life Orb Jolly 117-169. Rotom-W Sitrus Timid 100-151. Two Intimidate-immune mons (Annihilape, Dragapult) — use Incineroar carefully. Gholdengo is best Floette answer (resists Fairy 0.5x, Make It Rain SE 2x). Swampert Ice Punch 4x on Garchomp. Plan: lead non-rain, exhaust Altaria, bring rain late.

decisions.rationale: Cloud Nine Altaria dismantles Drizzle/Swift Swim. Floette Mega Fairy Aura sweeps with Light of Ruin; Energy Ball OHKOs Swampert. Garchomp EQ handles Gholdengo. Rotom-W Thunderbolt threatens Pelipper and provides second Will-O-Wisp. Altaria outspeeds entire foe team for fast Tailwind.
decisions.notebook: Opponent rain team: Pelipper Damp Rock, Mega Swampert Swift Swim, Gholdengo, Incineroar, Houndoom, Farigiraf. Cloud Nine is our hard counter. Gholdengo walls Floette and must be handled by Garchomp. Incineroar has Intimidate but our leads are special. Farigiraf Armor Tail blocks only opposing priority; Ally Switch is a mind-game tool.

decisions.rationale: Fake Out (+3 priority) guarantees flinching Altaria before Tailwind can go up — stopping their speed control is the top priority. Make It Rain hits both foes: 63-137% on Floette (possible OHKO) and 36-82% on Altaria (breaks Focus Sash). Even if Floette survives and hits Incineroar with Light of Ruin (33-53%), that's a favorable trade. Main risk is double Protect but that's passive and unlikely on their Mega + sash lead.

decisions.rationale: Protect (+4) outpaces Fake Out (+3), so Floette is safe regardless of target. Tailwind secures long-term speed control. Even if Fake Out flinches Altaria, Sash guarantees survival. Next turn we can Mega Evolve Floette and pivot to Garchomp or press attacks under Tailwind. Switching Altaria to Garchomp now risks Garchomp eating Fake Out and being flinched, wasting momentum.
decisions.notebook: Cloud Nine Altaria hard-counters their Damp Rock rain mode; preserve it to deny Swift Swim Mega Swampert. Gholdengo walls Floette—Garchomp is our primary Gholdengo answer. Incineroar Intimidate is irrelevant to our special leads. Farigiraf Armor Tail blocks only opposing priority; Ally Switch is a mind-game tool. Houndoom Flash Fire + Focus Sash may absorb Fire moves aimed at Gholdengo.

decisions.rationale: Flare Blitz on Floette can OHKO (39-126%) the opponent's Mega; Shadow Ball on Altaria can KO at 41% (30-82%), removing Cloud Nine. Splitting targets avoids overkill waste. Incineroar survives Light of Ruin + recoil thanks to Sitrus Berry. If both KO, field is cleared; if one KO, major progress either way.

Garchomp's EQ threatens the 53-162% OHKO range on Gholdengo while Altaria is immune to spread EQ. Opponent must respect the KO range: if Gholdengo stays and doesn't Protect, it likely faints. Rotom-Wash lacks this immediate pressure and lets Gholdengo Recover freely. Garchomp's 169 Speed also outruns both foes, giving us tempo.

decisions.rationale: Shadow Ball guarantees KO on 19% Altaria, removing Cloud Nine to enable Drizzle+Swift Swim plan. Incineroar must Protect at 39% HP—any SE hit KOs it. Gholdengo risks EQ (61-155%) but survives minimum rolls; if Garchomp uses Rock Slide/Dragon Claw/Protect, Gholdengo is safe. KOing Altaria now is worth the risk—letting it live means Roost to 70% or Tailwind for opponent speed control.

decisions.rationale: Garchomp EQ moves first (169 > all), OHKOs Incineroar before it acts, and Altaria is immune pre-Roost. Altaria then Roosts to 70% before Gholdengo's -2 Shadow Ball (17-28%). Even if both Protect, we get free recovery. Tailwind leaves Altaria vulnerable to Shadow Ball KO on a mid-high roll; switching loses Cloud Nine for the rain matchup. Roost+EQ is the safest and most consistent line.

Next turn: Pelipper Wide Guard blocks Garchomp spread moves while Swampert Ice Punches Altaria (4x SE KO at 47%), removing Cloud Nine to enable Drizzle+Swift Swim sweep.

decisions.rationale: EQ KOs Incineroar before it can Parting Shot (both 0 prio, Garchomp 169 > 112 max). Gholdengo almost certainly Protects (+4 prio). Tailwind exploits the free turn while Incineroar dies, giving 4 turns of speed control for the Rotom-Wash endgame. Altaria at 48% + Sash survives any single hit; Cloud Nine stays active to suppress Damp Rock rain if Pelipper comes in.

selection: Wide Guard (your side, including ally Swampert)
decisions.rationale: Wide Guard (pri +3) blocks Garchomp's Earthquake/Rock Slide (used EQ twice straight). Ice Punch 4x guaranteed KOs Altaria at 47% even across full range. Mega Evolving now sets Swift Swim for next turn once Cloud Nine is gone. Main risk: Garchomp Dragon Claw on Swampert (25-93%, possible KO at 42%), but opponent has patterned on Earthquake. If Altaria burns Swampert, halved 4x Ice Punch still likely KOs at 47%. KOing Altaria removes Cloud Nine and unlocks rain+Swift Swim mode.
decisions.notebook: Opponent team: Floette-Eternal Mega (Floettite, Timid 106-158) — fainted G1. Altaria Cloud Nine + Focus Sash (consumed) + Tailwind — primary rain counter; Sash gone at 47%. Plan: KO Altaria T5 to remove Cloud Nine; Mega Swampert Swift Swim in rain next turn (164-268 Spe). Opponent Tailwind expires in 2 turns. Gholdengo at 12% and Incineroar at 39% are fragile endgame pieces — preserve for late.

decisions.rationale: Incineroar is the only viable switch: Intimidate weakens Garchomp, Fake Out gives next-turn priority flinch, and 39% HP gives a chance to survive EQ through Atk drop. Gholdengo at 12% with -2 SpA is guaranteed dead to Earthquake and offers nothing. Preserve Gholdengo as a last-resort endgame piece.
decisions.notebook: Game 1 in dire shape: Swampert-Mega fainted, 3v5 (Pelipper/Incineroar/Gholdengo vs Altaria/Garchomp/Rotom-W/Annihilape/Dragapult). For G2-G3: Swampert Ice Punch 4x on Garchomp AND Altaria; Pelipper Wide Guard blocks Garchomp spread; must KO Altaria early to enable rain mode. Two Intimidate-immune foes (Annihilape Defiant, Dragapult ClearBody). Consider leading Swampert + Pelipper to rush Altaria with Ice Punch before Cloud Nine matters.

decisions.rationale: Roost heals Altaria to ~98% and removes Flying type, cutting Ice Punch from 4x OHKO to 2x survivable range. Garchomp Dragon Claw threatens to KO 41% Swampert before it can Ice Punch. If Swampert Protects, Altaria still safely heals. Preserves Cloud Nine rain suppression and keeps both offensive threats on field.

reflections.summary: Won because Gholdengo's Steel/Ghost typing resisted Altaria's Draco Meteor while Leftovers healing offset chip damage, letting Shadow Ball win the attrition war against Altaria's Roost stall. Altaria's Draco Meteor self-drops made it progressively weaker, and Good as Gold blocked Will-O-Wisp. Swampert-Mega, Pelipper, and Incineroar all fainted doing their jobs; Gholdengo cleaned up from turn 15 onward. The SpA -2 from earlier Make It Rain uses slowed the KO significantly but Leftovers + Recover
reflections.adjustment: Avoid Make It Rain entirely if Gholdengo is the planned endgame cleaner — at SpA -2 it took 8 Shadow Balls to KO a Roosting Altaria, nearly costing the game. Lead with Gholdengo against Altaria leads instead of Swampert+Pelipper rush, since Gholdengo already walls Altaria's entire set and preserves rain teammates for the backline (Annihilape, Dragapult). Consider bringing a different fourth if opponent keeps Altaria+Garchomp core, as Incineroar fainted without meaningful contribution.
reflections.notebook: G2-G3 plan: Gholdengo is the primary Altaria answer — resists Draco Meteor, immune to Will-O-Wisp via Good as Gold, Leftovers + Recover out-sustain Roost stall. Lead Gholdengo directly vs Altaria leads rather than spending Swampert-Mega/Pelipper. Avoid Make It Rain if Gholdengo needed for endgame (SpA -2 makes Shadow Ball take 8+ turns vs Roost Altaria). Shadow Ball is the safe neutral/SE chip throughout. Opponent Altaria: Focus Sash + Cloud Nine + Roost + Draco Meteor + Will-O-Wisp + Tailwind — pure stall, cannot threaten Gholdengo. Opponent backline: Annihilape (Jolly, Defiant, Leftovers, RageFist/DrainPunch/Taunt/Protect) — SE Rage Fist threatens Gholdengo, Taunt shuts Recover, Drain Punch IMMUNE vs Gholdengo. Dragapult (Jolly, ClearBody, MuscleBand, DragonDarts/Uturn/WillOWisp/Protect) — Darts NVE vs Gholdengo, Shadow Ball SE back. Gholdengo favorable vs both backline ghosts but must avoid Annihilape Taunt locking out Recover. Incineroar Intimidate dead weight vs Annihilape (Defiant) and Dragapult (ClearBody). Pelipper Wide Guard blocks Garchomp Earthquake/Rock Slide spread. Opponent punishes predictable Protect. KEY: Floette-Eternal (Floettite, FlowerVeil, Timid) unrevealed backline — Light of Ruin/Moonblast/EnergyBall/Protect; Gholdengo resists Moonblast, Make It Rain SE but self-drops SpA.

reflections.summary: Altaria was left as the final Pokémon against Gholdengo, which it cannot damage due to Good as Gold blocking Will-O-Wisp, Steel/Ghost resisting Draco Meteor, and Roost PP being depleted. Garchomp, the only team member with super-effective Ground coverage, fainted earlier, leaving no win condition.
reflections.adjustment: Preserve Garchomp (or bring another Ground/Fire attacker) specifically to handle Gholdengo. Avoid positioning Altaria as the last Pokémon; if Garchomp is lost, use Floette-Eternal or Rotom-Wash to pressure Gholdengo earlier with neutral hits before SpA drops accumulate.
reflections.notebook: Opponent's Gholdengo (Modest, Leftovers, Shadow Ball/Make It Rain/Protect/Recover) is a bulky win condition that must be answered with super-effective Ground or Fire moves. Garchomp's Earthquake is the primary check; keep it healthy. Altaria's Cloud Nine disrupts rain but is helpless vs Gholdengo endgame. Incineroar (Careful, Sitrus, Fake Out/Parting Shot/Flare Blitz/Protect) pivots and cycles Intimidate. Pelipper (Damp Rock) sets rain and Tailwind; Swampert-Mega is standard physical rain sweeper. Unrevealed Farigiraf (Armor Tail, Lum Berry) likely runs Ally Switch/Helping Hand; Houndoom (Flash Fire, Focus Sash) may absorb Fire moves. For game 2, prioritize Gholdengo removal and consider leading Garchomp to apply immediate pressure.
